A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the higher concentration ascorbic acid in the solution leads to the higher degradation rate of the investigated colorants and the higher degradation rate leads to a lower half-life.
the higher concentration ascorbic acid in the presence of azo food colorants leads to a higher rate constant and a shorter time of colorant degradation.
the presence of ascorbic acids leads to the faster degradation of the investigated azo dyes and the higher concentration of the ascorbic acids results in the higher degradation rate of the colorants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of ascorbic acids in food colorants leads to their degradation.
the presence of ascorbic in the food can lead to a faster colorant degradation, which can be a reason of the colorant loss and, consequently, of the food coloration change.
the presence of ascorbic acids in foods can accelerate the degradation of artificial food colorants.
